You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task task-5c5f9006 (unresolved; 8 wrong submissions)

## Demos observed
Task family: mostly uniform background, two solid colored bars/segments on edges (different orientations/positions), isolated dots of another color. Output recolors dots to 4 and draws beam/fill shapes matching dot(s) original color from edge bars. Need infer precise rule carefully. Prior rule guesses about ray columns were wrong.

### Demo 1 (8x27, bg1)
Bars: top r0 c12-14 color7; bottom r7 c24-26 color7. Single-color dots 0 at r2c13 and r5c14.
Output: dots become 4. Top beam of 0 is vertical in c13 from r1-r2 (ending at dot), and c14 from r1-r5? Actual output rows1-5 c14=0 except dot at r5 c14=4. Bottom beam of 0 appears c25,c26 rows1-6 (both columns). There are subtle details, record raw pair from conversation if needed.

### Demo 2 (12x11, bg7)
Bars: top-left r0 c0-1 color2; bottom r11 c6-7 color2. Dots color8 at r2c7 and r6c6.
Output: dots become4. Left edge bar extends down two rows originally (r0 cols0,1) and outputs color8 filling cols0-1 rows1-10. Another apparent vertical 8 region in cols6-7 rows3-10 from bottom bar, with dots 4 at locations r2c7 and r6c6 (inspect exact output in transcript). This demonstrates rectangular wedges/stripes rather than simple rays, tied to dot positions.

### Demo 3 (24x26, bg7)
Bars top r0 c6-10 color8; bottom r23 c0-4 color8. Three dots color1: r8c8, r13c9, r17c10. Output dots become4. Output fills a broad rectangle in cols2-4 for rows0-22 (blue/1); and cols8-10 for rows1-17 with conditional stair-step narrowing: rows1-7 cols8-10=1; row8 c8=4, c9-10=1; rows9-12 c9-10=1; row13 c9=4 c10=1; rows14-16 c10=1; row17 c10=4. The bars lengths and number/positions of dots are important; rays/regions defined by projection, with steps where dots lie. Top and bottom segments seem to launch blocks with widths equal to segment length and position selected by point/direction, not simply rightmost N columns.

### Demo 4 (18x21, bg2)
Left vertical bar c0 rows9-10 color1; right vertical bar c20 rows16-17 color1. Dot color0 at r10c10. Output: row10 c1-9 are 0, dot becomes4. Bottom row r17 c0-19 are 0, right bar retained. Thus edge bars extend inward along same row(s) or form projections, dot matters: horizontal line from left beam up to dot. This is unlike simplistic vertical-only rule.

### Demo 5 (21x6, bg3)
Left vertical bar c0 rows7-11 color9; right bar c5 rows16-20 color9. Three dots color8: r9c4, r10c4, r11c3. Output dot cells become4; r9-10 c1-3 are 8; r11 c1-2 are 8. Also rows18-20 c0-4 become8 (filling from bottom-left across), right bar preserved. Again rays/rectangular fill based on edge bars/dots.

## Test input
23x17 bg3. Top bar r0 c13-16 color6 (length4); bottom bar r22 c6-9 color6 (length4). Dots color1 at r5c7, r18c9, r20c8. No output accepted; 8/8 wrong submissions. Most attempts incorrectly drew vertical continuous stripes in selected columns; other tries included bottom-side region and stripe but inaccurate. Do NOT reuse prior submissions as correct.

## General inference
Pattern likely projects filled rectangles/lines from colored edge segments toward/through dot coordinates, output dot cells recolored 4; edge color bars remain. Dots seem determine positions where beam boundaries step/change width. Orientation can be horizontal and vertical. Need derive ARC task rule from the exact demonstrations before submit; avoid oversimplifying into “rays one per dot in rightmost bar columns.”
